title: Perfekt Tense (The Spoken Past)
description: Learn how to talk about the past in everyday spoken German using 'haben' or 'sein' plus a Past Participle.
conjugationTable: Regular verbs: ge + stem + t (gemacht, gespielt)
Irregular verbs: ge + stem + en (gesehen, getrunken)
errorTraps: The helping verb (haben/sein) is in position 2, but the past participle MUST go to the very end of the sentence.

title: Präteritum of Modal Verbs, Sein, and Haben
description: While Perfekt is for most verbs, Modal verbs, sein, and haben prefer the simple past (Präteritum) even in spoken German.
conjugationTable: sein -> war, warst, war, waren, wart, waren
haben -> hatte, hattest, hatte, hatten, hattet, hatten
können -> konnte, müssen -> musste, wollen -> wollte
errorTraps: Modal verbs lose their umlauts in the Präteritum (müssen -> musste).

title: The Dative Case
description: An introduction to the third German case. The Dative marks the indirect object (the receiver of an action).

examples.german: Ich gebe dem Mann das Buch.
examples.english: I give the man the book.

errorTraps: In the plural dative, you must add an '-n' to the end of the noun (den Kindern, den Freunden).

title: Dative Prepositions
description: Prepositions that always force the following noun into the Dative case.
errorTraps: Mnemonic: 'Aus, außer, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu' ALWAYS take Dative!

title: Two-Way Prepositions (Wechselpräpositionen)
description: Prepositions that take Accusative for movement/direction (Wohin?) and Dative for location (Wo?).

examples.german: Ich lege das Buch auf den Tisch.
examples.english: I lay the book onto the table. (Accusative/Movement)

examples.german: Das Buch liegt auf dem Tisch.
examples.english: The book lies on the table. (Dative/Location)

conjugationTable: in, an, auf, neben, hinter, über, unter, vor, zwischen
errorTraps: Movement must be directed towards a destination to trigger Accusative. Running around IN a park is still Dative (location).

title: Verbs that take the Dative
description: Some verbs don't take a direct object (Accusative). Instead, they strictly require a Dative object.

examples.english: How are you? (How goes it to you?)
The man likes the car. (The car is pleasing to the man.)

errorTraps: With 'gefallen', the thing you like is the subject, and YOU are the dative object! (Der Pullover gefällt mir).

title: Personal Pronouns in the Dative Case
description: How to say 'to me', 'to you', 'to him', etc.
errorTraps: Do not confuse 'ihr' (to her) with 'ihr' (you all / their). Context is key!

title: Coordinating Conjunctions
description: Connectors that do not change the word order of the sentence (Position 0).

examples.german: Ich bin müde, aber ich lerne.
examples.english: I am tired, but I study.

examples.german: Ich trinke Tee, denn ich bin krank.
examples.english: I drink tea, because I am sick.

errorTraps: These conjunctions count as 'Position 0', meaning the very next word is Position 1, and the verb is safely in Position 2.

title: Subordinating Conjunctions (weil, dass, wenn)
description: Connectors that kick the conjugated verb to the very end of the sentence.

examples.german: Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil es regnet.
examples.english: I am staying home because it is raining.
I know that you are coming.

errorTraps: The verb MUST go to the absolute end of the clause. '...weil ich krank BIN' (NOT 'weil ich bin krank').

title: Comparison of Adjectives
description: Forming the comparative (more) and superlative (most) forms of adjectives.
errorTraps: Use 'als' for comparisons (schneller ALS) and 'wie' for equals (so schnell WIE).

title: Reflexive Verbs and Pronouns
description: Verbs where the subject and the object are the same (e.g. I wash myself).
errorTraps: In German, many more verbs are reflexive than in English, like 'sich freuen' (to be happy/rejoice) or 'sich treffen' (to meet).

title: Adjective Endings in Dative & Accusative
description: Expanding adjective declension to the other cases.

examples.german: Ich spiele mit dem kleinen Kind.
examples.english: I play with the small child. (Dative)

conjugationTable: Accusative Definite: den großen (M), die große (F), das große (N), die großen (Pl)
Dative Definite: ALL endings are -EN! (dem großen, der großen, dem großen, den großen)
errorTraps: In the Dative case, adjective endings after an article (definite or indefinite) are ALWAYS '-en'.

title: Konjunktiv II (Polite Requests)
description: Using 'would' and 'could' to make polite requests.
conjugationTable: haben -> hätte, hättest, hätte, hätten, hättet, hätten
sein -> wäre, wärst, wäre, wären, wärt, wären
errorTraps: These behave exactly like modal verbs: 'Würden Sie mir das Salz GEBEN?' (main verb at the end).

title: Sentence Order: TeKaMoLo
description: When multiple elements are in a sentence, German prefers a specific order: Time, Cause, Manner, Place.

examples.german: Ich fahre heute wegen des Regens schnell nach Hause.
examples.english: I am driving home fast today because of the rain.

errorTraps: Time usually comes first. 'Ich spiele heute Fußball' is much more natural than 'Ich spiele Fußball heute'.

title: Verbs with Fixed Prepositions
description: Some verbs are forever bound to specific prepositions, which then dictate the case of the object.

examples.english: I am waiting for you. (warten + auf + Acc)
She dreams of a house. (träumen + von + Dat)

conjugationTable: warten auf (+ Acc) - to wait for
denken an (+ Acc) - to think about
sprechen über (+ Acc) - to talk about
träumen von (+ Dat) - to dream of
helfen bei (+ Dat) - to help with
errorTraps: You cannot translate these literally from English. 'Wait FOR' becomes 'warten AUF' (wait ON).
